name: mbedtls

patches.replace: /* #define MBEDTLS_NET_C -- disabled for this port, see mbedtls.json's notes */
patches.reason: library/net_sockets.c's portable (non-_WIN32) path needs a fuller BSD-sockets surface than this PAL currently exposes -- confirmed by a real build attempt, not assumed: select()/fd_set/FD_ZERO/FD_SET/FD_ISSET/suseconds_t/SO_TYPE all came back as undeclared on Windows. This is squarely curl's territory (the next port in this queue, which genuinely needs sockets), not this crypto-only first pass -- mbedtls's own SSL/TLS layer only calls into net_sockets.c through the mbedtls_net_context callback shape a *consumer* can already swap out for its own I/O, so disabling MBEDTLS_NET_C does not block AES/SHA/RSA/etc. use at all, only the convenience BSD-socket helper this port's own test doesn't use.

notes: Next in the porting matrix expansion queue after bzip2/xz/pcre2 (see TODO.md's "Porting matrix expansion" bullet). Picked the 3.6.7 LTS release (supported through at least March 2027), not the newer 4.2.0: 4.2.0 dropped the plain top-level Makefile entirely in favor of a CMake-only build, and this project's tooling (tools/crt-port-build.py) has no CMake-driven-port support at all -- 3.6.7 still ships a real, hand-written top-level Makefile.

skip_configure (a new build.system:"configure" flag, added this session to tools/crt-port-build.py's build_configure_port()) -- mbedtls has no ./configure step at all; everything else in the configure-based flow (patches, env/CFLAGS overrides, make_args/install_args, Windows shell wrapping, parallel -jN jobs) is reused unchanged, so this only skips the one step that doesn't apply rather than adding a whole separate 'system' type for one recipe.

install_args (new: a base build.install_args field, distinct from target_overrides.<os>.make_args, extra arguments specific to `make install` only) carries mbedtls's own DESTDIR=@PORT_PREFIX@ install convention -- unlike every other recipe here, mbedtls's Makefile uses `make install DESTDIR=...` (installing straight into DESTDIR, not a staging root prepended to a separate --prefix=), not autotools' --prefix= convention.

make_args: ["lib"] targets the top-level Makefile's `lib` goal specifically (`$(MAKE) -C library`, which itself defaults to `static` only unless the `SHARED` make variable is set -- see library/Makefile's `ifndef SHARED / all: static / else / all: shared static / endif`), not the default `all` goal (`programs tests`). This also sidesteps the framework/exported.make submodule requirement entirely: the top-level Makefile's own conditional only requires it for goals other than `lib`/`library/%` (`ifneq (,$(filter-out lib library/%,$(or $(MAKECMDGOALS),all)))`), and this tarball release does vendor a populated framework/ directory, but there is no reason to depend on it for a library-only port.

install_args' `-o no_test -o programs -o mbedtls_test` (GNU Make's --old-file/--assume-old option, one per phony prerequisite) routes around a real dependency-chain problem: mbedtls's own `install: no_test` -> `no_test: programs` -> `programs: lib mbedtls_test` chain means a plain `make install` would also try to build every example program under programs/ and the whole mbedtls_test framework (needing framework/exported.make for real this time, and pulling in far more than a library-only port needs). `-o` tells make to treat each of those phony targets as already up to date, so make walks straight to install:'s own recipe body (a handful of mkdir -p/cp -rp/cp -RP commands) without touching its prerequisites at all. Verified directly with GNU Make 4.2.1 (WSL Ubuntu 20.04, native, not yet through this project's own toolchain): `make -n install -o no_test -o programs -o mbedtls_test DESTDIR=...` shows only the install: recipe's own copy commands, no rebuild of programs/mbedtls_test; a real `make lib` + `make install ... DESTDIR=...` run produced exactly `include/{mbedtls,psa}`, `lib/lib{mbedtls,mbedx509,mbedcrypto}.a`, and (harmlessly) a handful of `bin/*.sh` helper scripts that upstream's own tarball ships with the executable bit already set (the `for p in programs/*/*` loop in install:'s recipe only copies files that are `[ -x $p ]`, which excludes ordinary un-built .c/.h sources when programs/ was never compiled -- confirmed by extracting a clean tarball natively into a Linux filesystem, since a first attempt copying from an NTFS-mounted WSL path falsely reported every file as executable, an artifact of that filesystem bridge, not the real tarball).

target_overrides.windows.cflags undefines _WIN32/_WIN32_WCE/__WIN32__/WIN32/__MINGW32__ (the same technique as every other Windows recipe here) and additionally defines __unix__: unlike the other ports so far, two of mbedtls's own library sources (entropy_poll.c, timing.c) have a HARD #error (not just a silently-empty translation unit) if neither _WIN32 nor a recognized Unix-like macro (unix/__unix/__unix__/__APPLE__+__MACH__/__HAIKU__/__midipix__, see library/common.h's MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_IS_UNIXLIKE derivation) is defined -- since this PAL has no real <windows.h>/<bcrypt.h>/QueryPerformanceCounter to satisfy the _WIN32 branch anyway (same reasoning as every prior port's _WIN32 undef), the correct fix is routing them down their portable POSIX branch (getrandom()/fopen("/dev/urandom") for entropy, gettimeofday() for timing) via -D__unix__, not leaving _WIN32 defined and hoping the Windows branch compiles.

MBEDTLS_NET_C (networking, on by default) is disabled via the patch above -- first attempted leaving it enabled (with _WIN32 undefined, expecting library/net_sockets.c to take the same portable POSIX sockets path <sys/socket.h>/<netinet/in.h>/<arpa/inet.h>/<netdb.h> this project's own libc/src/socket.c and tests/socket_network_test.c already exercise on all three OSes), but a real Windows build attempt showed this PAL's <sys/socket.h>/friends don't yet expose the fuller BSD-sockets surface net_sockets.c also needs (select()/fd_set/FD_ZERO/FD_SET/FD_ISSET/suseconds_t/SO_TYPE all came back undeclared) -- see the patch's own "reason" for the full explanation and why disabling it doesn't block AES/SHA/RSA/etc. use (mbedtls's SSL/TLS layer only touches net_sockets.c through the mbedtls_net_context callback shape a consumer can already swap for its own I/O). Revisit once curl (the next port in this queue, which genuinely needs sockets) has driven this PAL's socket surface further.

Only mbedtls's own library/ static build is in scope for this first pass (no `programs`, no `tests`/mbedtls_test, no shared build): mbedtls's own Windows shared-library link rules (library/Makefile's `libmbedcrypto.dll`/etc. targets) hardcode `-lws2_32 -lwinmm -lgdi32`, real Windows SDK import libraries this PAL does not provide -- deferred, matching bzip2/xz/pcre2's own precedent of starting static-only and adding a shared-build entry only once the static build is verified solid.

porting/tests/mbedtls_crypto_test.c is a real cryptographic round trip, not a version-string/link-only smoke check: SHA-256("abc") compared against the actual NIST/FIPS 180-4 known-answer digest, plus a full AES-128-CBC encrypt/decrypt round trip verifying the decrypted output exactly reproduces the original plaintext (and that the ciphertext is not simply equal to the plaintext, so a no-op 'encrypt' couldn't accidentally pass). Verified natively first (WSL Ubuntu 20.04, plain gcc, against a native `make lib` + `make install DESTDIR=...` build) before wiring into this recipe/tools/crt-port-build.py at all, to separate 'does the API usage make sense' from 'does the CRT toolchain integration work'.

Verified for real through this project's own toolchain end to end, both static-only: Windows (`cmake --build --preset windows-host-ninja-debug --target port-test-mbedtls`, real x86_64 host) and Linux (WSL Ubuntu 20.04 + clang-18, `cmake --build --preset linux-host-ninja-debug --target port-test-mbedtls` in a clean clone) both build the full library/ tree, install headers+libs via the DESTDIR/`-o`-skip install path described above, and print `mbedtls_crypto_test: ok sha256=ba7816bf8f01cfea... aes128cbc=roundtrip-ok`. Also reran this project's full Windows ctest suite afterward (83/83 passed) to confirm the tools/crt-port-build.py changes (skip_configure, install_args) didn't regress any existing port or PAL test. macOS not yet verified (no local macOS hardware this session) -- both static-pass on Linux/Windows, macOS: untested.
